questions.question: At what rate of interest (rounded off to two decimal places) per year will a sum of money double itself in 12 years on simple interest?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

For a sum to become **n times** itself at **Simple Interest**, use the shortcut: **Rate (R) = (n − 1) ÷ T × 100**.

Here, the sum **doubles**, so **n = 2**, and time **T = 12 years**.

R = (2 − 1) ÷ 12 × 100

R = 100 ÷ 12 = 8.333...

**∴ The correct answer is 8.33%.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time (T) = **12 years**

Final Amount (A) = **2 × Principal (P)**

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b100a3effb31f726626d88e2ff34d32487ceb81bea273cc99252cc2986285709.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let **Principal (P)** = ₹100

⇒ Since the sum doubles, **Amount (A)** = 2 × 100 = **₹200**

⇒ **Simple Interest (SI)** = Amount − Principal = 200 − 100 = **₹100**

⇒ Substitute in the formula: 100 = (100 × R × 12) ÷ 100

⇒ 100 = 12 × R

⇒ R = 100 ÷ 12

⇒ R = 8.333... ≈ **8.33%**

**∴ The correct answer is 8.33%.**

**__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest Definition

Simple interest is calculated only on the **original principal** amount for every time period.

Sum tripling rule

If a sum triples (n=3), the interest gained is 2P, so **R × T = 200**.

Amount calculation

Final Amount (A) = Principal (P) + SI = **P[1 + (R × T) ÷ 100]**.

questions.question: The difference between the compound interest, compounded annually and the simple interest if ₹47,100 is deposited at 9% rate of interest per annum for 2 years is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For a period of **2 years**, the difference between **Compound Interest (CI)** and **Simple Interest (SI)** is given by the formula:

**Difference (D) = P × (R/100)²**

D = 47,100 × (9/100) × (9/100)

D = 471 × 81 / 100 ⇒ 38,151 / 100 = 381.51

**∴ The correct answer is ₹381.51.**

**Given:**

**Principal (P)** = ₹47,100

⇒ SI = (P × R × T) / 100

⇒ SI = (47,100 × 9 × 2) / 100

⇒ SI = 471 × 18 = ₹8,478

**Step 2: Calculate Compound Interest (CI)**

⇒ Amount (A) = P × (1 + R/100)T

⇒ A = 47,100 × (1 + 9/100)²

⇒ A = 47,100 × (1.09)²

⇒ A = 47,100 × 1.1881 = ₹55,959.51

⇒ CI = Amount − Principal = 55,959.51 − 47,100 = ₹8,859.51

**Step 3: Calculate the Difference**

⇒ Difference = CI − SI

⇒ Difference = 8,859.51 − 8,478 = ₹381.51

**∴ The correct answer is ₹381.51.**

CI − SI Difference for 3 Years

Effective Rate Method

For 2 years, the effective CI rate is [x + y + (xy/100)]%. The difference between effective CI and SI rates is exactly (R²/100)%.

Compounding Periods

If interest is compounded half-yearly, the rate is halved (R/2) and the time is doubled (2T) for calculation purposes.

Compounding Half-Yearly Rule

Effective Rate of Interest

The effective rate for two successive periods of r% is given by [r + r + (r × r)/100]%. For 4%, it is 4 + 4 + 0.16 = 8.16%.

Compound Interest Formula

CI = Amount − Principal = P[(1 + R/100)ⁿ − 1].

questions.question: At what rate of interest (in percentage) per year will a sum of money double itself in 5 years on simple interest?

**Given:**

Time (T) = **5 years**

Let **Principal (P)** = ₹100

Since the money doubles, **Amount (A)** = 2 × 100 = **₹200**

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = **Amount (A) − Principal (P)**

SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5446fb4813a4971feb7245cfaa388abd4975e9c3598f1062a6632b299996b543.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ SI = 200 − 100 = 100

⇒ 100 = (100 × R × 5) ÷ 100

⇒ 100 = 5 × R

⇒ R = 100 ÷ 5

⇒ R = 20%

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum of money n-times itself

If a sum becomes n-times itself in T years at SI, then **R = 100(n − 1) ÷ T**.

Compound Interest Doubling (Rule of 72)

To find the approximate time to double money at CI, use **T ≈ 72 ÷ R**.

Difference between SI and CI

Difference for 2 years = **P(R ÷ 100)²**.

questions.question: Find the simple interest (in ₹) if a sum of ₹350 is borrowed for 1.5 years at 20% per annum rate of interest.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Net Interest Rate = **Rate** × **Time**

Net Rate = 20% × 1.5 = 30%

**Simple Interest** = 30% of **Principal** (₹350)

⇒ 30/100 × 350 = 3 × 35 = 105

**∴ The correct answer is ₹105.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Principal (P)** = ₹350

**Rate (R)** = 20% per annum

**Time (T)** = 1.5 years

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/63b284e281df2153be501c55e2d1db8a611c1846e04aaf2d5b6d55e655e3ed3f.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ SI = (350 × 20 × 1.5) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = (350 × 30) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = 35 × 3

⇒ SI = 105

**∴ The correct answer is ₹105.**

**__Additional Information__**

Total Amount Formula

The total amount (A) to be paid back is the sum of the **Principal** and the **Simple Interest**: A = P + SI.

Constant Interest Property

In **Simple Interest**, the interest remains constant for every year as it is always calculated on the original **Principal**.

Rate of Interest Calculation

If the interest is known, the rate can be found using R = (SI × 100) ÷ (P × T).

questions.question: The difference between the compound interest, compounded annually and the simple interest if ₹17,700 is deposited at 4% rate of interest per annum for 2 years is:

For a period of **2 years**, the difference (D) between **Compound Interest** and **Simple Interest** is given by the formula: D = P × (R/100)².

Given: **Principal (P)** = ₹17,700 and **Rate (R)** = 4%.

⇒ Difference = 17,700 × (4/100) × (4/100)

⇒ Difference = 17,700 × 16 / 10,000

⇒ Difference = 177 × 16 / 100 = 2832 / 100 = ₹28.32

**∴ The correct answer is ₹28.32.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Principal (P) = ₹17,700, Rate (R) = 4% p.a., Time (n) = 2 years.

**Formula Used:**

1. Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) / 100

2. Amount (A) = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ

3. Compound Interest (CI) = A − P

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/dcedb930bfe6f2ed956957432dcde6bd79b03d28c0e3b1043f717405c40ea819.png] 

**Step-by-step Calculation:**

⇒ SI = 177 × 8 = ₹1,416

⇒ CI for 1st year = 4% of 17,700 = ₹708

⇒ CI for 2nd year = 708 + (4% of 708)

⇒ Interest on 1st year interest = 708 × 0.04 = ₹28.32

⇒ Total CI = 708 + 708 + 28.32 = ₹1,444.32

⇒ Difference = CI − SI = 1,444.32 − 1,416 = ₹28.32

**∴ The correct answer is ₹28.32.**

Difference for 3 Years

The difference between CI and SI for 3 years is calculated as: D = P(R/100)² × (3 + R/100).

Effective Rate of Interest

For 2 years, the effective CI rate is R + R + (R×R)/100. For 4%, it is 4 + 4 + 0.16 = 8.16%, while SI is 8%.

First Year Interest

When compounded annually, the Simple Interest and Compound Interest for the **first year** are always equal.

Total units = 11 + 10 = 21 units → ₹1,218.

Total Principal (P) = ₹1,218

Rate of Interest (r) = **10%** p.a. compounded annually.

⇒ A = M × (1.1)¹² ÷ (1.1)¹¹

⇒ A = M × 1.1 = M × 11/10

⇒ A/M = 11/10

⇒ Total ratio sum = 11 + 10 = 21 units

⇒ 21 units = 1218

⇒ 1 unit = 1218 ÷ 21 = 58

⇒ Mahesh's share (M) = 10 units = 10 × 58

Compound Interest Formula

The amount **A** after **n** years is given by A = P(1 + r/100)ⁿ, where **P** is the principal and **r** is the annual interest rate.

Equal Amounts Case

When two people receive the same amount at the same rate but for different times **t₁** and **t₂**, the ratio of their principals is inverse to the ratio of their accumulation factors: P₁/P₂ = (1 + r/100)⁽t² − t¹⁾.

Compounding annually is a form of **successive percentage increase** where the base changes every year.

questions.question: Rishi has ₹1,612 with him. He divided it amongst his sons Shan and Piyush and asked them to invest it at 8% rate of interest per annum, compounded annually. It was seen that Shan and Piyush got the same amount after 19 and 20 years, respectively. How much (in ₹) did Rishi give to Shan?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Shan's share (S)** to **Piyush's share (P)** is given by (1 + R/100)Δt : 1.

Here, difference in time (Δt) = 20 − 19 = 1 year and Rate (R) = 8%.

Ratio S : P = (1 + 8/100)¹ : 1 ⇒ 108 : 100 ⇒ 27 : 25.

Total units = 27 + 25 = 52 units → ₹1,612.

1 unit = 1612 ÷ 52 = ₹31.

**Shan's share** = 27 × 31 = ₹837.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹837.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total Principal = **₹1,612** | Rate (R) = **8% p.a.**

Time for **Shan** (n₁) = **19 years** | Time for **Piyush** (n₂) = **20 years**.

**Formula Used:**

Amount (A) = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e90e2f39558c447e384a5e5838c968db76963e3df06033c22ee2b701d6b48c20.png] 

Let the amount given to **Shan** be S and to **Piyush** be P.

⇒ S(1 + 8/100)¹⁹ = P(1 + 8/100)²⁰

⇒ S = P(1 + 8/100)²⁰−¹⁹

⇒ S = P(108/100)

⇒ S/P = 27/25

⇒ S = [27 / (27 + 25)] × 1612

⇒ S = (27 / 52) × 1612

⇒ S = 27 × 31

⇒ S = **₹837**

questions.question: How much will a sum of ₹60,000 become after one year if the interest is compounded half-yearly at 18% per annum compound interest?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For **half-yearly compounding**, the rate becomes half and the number of periods doubles.

Rate (r) = 18% ÷ 2 = 9% per half-year | Time (n) = 1 × 2 = 2 periods.

**Net effective interest rate** for 2 periods = 9 + 9 + (9 × 9)/100 = 18.81%.

Total Amount = 100% (Principal) + 18.81% (Interest) = 118.81% of Principal.

Amount = 60,000 × 1.1881 = ₹71,286.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹71,286.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Principal (P) = **₹60,000**

Annual Rate (R) = **18% per annum**

Time (T) = **1 year**

**Formula Used:**

**Calculations:**

⇒ r = 18 ÷ 2 = 9% (Rate for 6 months)

⇒ n = 1 × 2 = 2 (Two half-year periods in 1 year)

⇒ A = 60,000 × (1 + 9/100)²

⇒ A = 60,000 × (109/100) × (109/100)

⇒ A = 6 × 109 × 109

⇒ A = 6 × 11881

⇒ A = ₹71,286

**∴ The correct answer is ₹71,286.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effective Rate of Interest

For two successive cycles of r%, the net percentage change is given by (x + y + xy/100)%. Here, 9 + 9 + (9×9)/100 = 18.81%.

For **Quarterly** compounding, Rate = R/4 and n = 4T. For **Monthly** compounding, Rate = R/12 and n = 12T.

Difference between CI and SI

For 2 years (or 2 cycles), the difference between Compound Interest and Simple Interest is P(r/100)².
